question: On 28 October 2026, the collision between two high-speed trains in Urda (Toledo) led to at least 69 deaths, following a failure of the LZB protection system. This is the second fatal accident on the Madrid-Seville line, which was classified as ‘obsolete’ by the European Commission in 2023.

In 2021, ADIF Alta Velocidad – the second largest recipient of NextGenerationEU funds in Spain – awarded a contract financed by the Recovery and Resilience Facility (C6.I1) to replace the LZB system with the European ERTMS system, which was scheduled to become operational in 2026. However, LZB was still in use on the day of the accident.

In 2026, Spain submitted documentation to prove its fulfilment of milestone 87 of its recovery and resilience plan, on railway modernisation contracts, including signalling and control actions. In light of the above: 1.

Did the Spanish Government include the Madrid-Seville ERTMS contract among the actions declared to confirm it had met milestone 87, thus unlocking disbursement of EU funds, which deliverables did it declare completed and with what documentation?
Does the Commission consider the implementation of the ERTMS deployment contract to have been proven despite the system not being operational?
What EU funding has Spain received for high-speed rail, by instrument, beneficiary and action, distinguishing between amounts granted, disbursed and actually implemented?
